text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Signalling the government's seriousness in promoting public transport, particularly the light rail transit, the Cabinet has ruled that new buildings need not allocate parking bays while existing buildings can reduce theirs.

-- Malaysians investing in China are advised to stay away from the gaming sector as the Chinese government has a policy of discouraging gambling, Deputy International Trade and Industry Minister Kerk Choo Ting said.
-- Dormitories may be built in the Klang Valley in Kuala Lumpur to provide cheap and decent accommodation for unmarried workers.

-- Ekran Bhd has stressed that it wants foreign financing for the Bakun dam, quashing recent speculation that the project's shares would not be offered to foreign investors because of their alleged lukewarm response.
-- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange is expected to go completely scripless, including derivatives, by the middle of this year.

-- Banks and financial institutions have asked for more time to submit concrete plans to Bank Negara on ways to comply with the new guidelines on lending to the property sector and for the purchase of stocks and shares.
